title: The Consumer Protection Act, 2019 - section 2, consumer definition
issuing_authority: Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution, Government of India
text: Section 2(7) defines a consumer to include a person who buys goods or hires or avails services for consideration, including certain approved users or beneficiaries, and excludes goods obtained for resale or commercial purpose and services availed for commercial purpose, subject to statutory qualifications and exceptions.

title: The Consumer Protection Act, 2019 - section 35, manner of making a complaint
issuing_authority: Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution, Government of India
text: Section 35 says a complaint may be filed with a District Commission by the consumer, a recognised consumer association (whether or not the consumer is a member), one or more consumers with the Commission's permission where numerous consumers share an interest, or specified governments or authorities. It also provides for electronic filing in the prescribed manner.

title: The Consumer Protection Act, 2019 - section 38, complaint procedure
issuing_authority: Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution, Government of India
text: Section 38(2)(a) states that, for a complaint relating to goods, the District Commission refers a copy of the admitted complaint to the opposite party within 21 days and directs them to provide their version within 30 days. The Commission may grant an extension of up to 15 days.

title: The Consumer Protection Act, 2019 - section 69, limitation period
issuing_authority: Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution, Government of India
text: Section 69 states that a consumer complaint must be filed within two years from the date the cause of action arises. The Commission may entertain a later complaint if sufficient cause for delay is shown and it records its reasons for condoning the delay.

title: The Right to Information Act, 2005 - section 6, request for information
issuing_authority: Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions, Government of India
text: Section 6 allows a person seeking information to make a written or electronic request in English, Hindi, or the official language of the area, with the prescribed fee, to the relevant Central or State Public Information Officer or Assistant Public Information Officer. The request must specify the information sought.

title: The Right to Information Act, 2005 - section 7, disposal of request
issuing_authority: Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions, Government of India
text: Section 7(1) states that the Central or State Public Information Officer should respond as expeditiously as possible and ordinarily within thirty days after receiving a section 6 request. Where the requested information concerns a person's life or liberty, the stated period is forty-eight hours. Other provisions and exceptions may apply.

title: The Right to Information Act, 2005 - section 8, exemptions from disclosure
issuing_authority: Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions, Government of India
text: Section 8 lists categories of information for which disclosure is exempt, including specified information affecting India's sovereignty, security, or relations with foreign states; information barred from publication by a court or tribunal; legislative privilege; and certain third-party commercial information, subject to statutory conditions and exceptions.

title: The Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 - section 3, domestic violence
issuing_authority: Ministry of Women and Child Development, Government of India
text: Section 3 describes domestic violence to include conduct that harms or endangers an aggrieved person's physical or mental health, safety, life, limb, or well-being. It includes physical, sexual, verbal, emotional, and economic abuse, and specified harassment or threats; the complete statutory definition and explanations govern.

title: The Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 - section 17, shared household
issuing_authority: Ministry of Women and Child Development, Government of India
text: Section 17 states that every woman in a domestic relationship has a right to reside in the shared household, whether or not she has a right, title, or beneficial interest in it. An aggrieved person may not be evicted or excluded by the respondent except in accordance with the procedure established by law.

title: The Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 - section 18, protection orders
issuing_authority: Ministry of Women and Child Development, Government of India
text: Section 18 allows a Magistrate, after giving the parties an opportunity to be heard and being prima facie satisfied that domestic violence has occurred or is likely, to issue a protection order. The section describes conduct that may be prohibited; the order and statutory conditions are determined by the Magistrate.

title: The Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 - section 19, residence orders
issuing_authority: Ministry of Women and Child Development, Government of India
text: Section 19 allows a Magistrate, when satisfied that domestic violence has taken place, to make specified residence orders. These include restraining dispossession from a shared household and other directions described in the section; the outcome depends on the application, evidence, and statutory requirements.

title: The Constitution of India - Articles 14, 15, 16 and 29(2)
issuing_authority: Legislative Department, Ministry of Law and Justice, Government of India
text: Article 14 guarantees equality before law and equal protection of the laws to every person. Article 15(1) bars the State from discriminating against citizens only on specified grounds, including race; Article 15(2) addresses access to specified public places. Article 16(2) bars discrimination in employment or appointment to an office under the State on listed grounds including race. Article 29(2) bars denial of admission to educational institutions maintained by the State or receiving State aid only on specified grounds, including race and language.
